newsitem.title: USA: Nazis moved "assets" into Switzerland to save party.
newsitem.headline: Nazis moved "assets" into Switzerland to save party.

text.p: The Nazi party moved massive amounts of money and documents into Switzerland near the end of the Second World War as part of a clandestine plan to keep its movement alive after Germany's defeat, according to a previously secret U.S. document released on Monday.

The document from the Office of Strategic Services, the precursor to the Central Intelligence Agency, said, "These funds are intended to organise and support the Nazi movement after the defeat of Germany as well as to encourage sympathies throughout Europe."

The May 9, 1945, memorandum added that to help the Nazi plan, the German government dissolved a government watchdog agency that would have prevented it from seizing assets inside Germany and moving it out of the country.
The two-page document -- complete with names of suspected Nazi agents and dated a day after Germany surrendered -- was released by the World Jewish Congress.

WJC researchers have been combing the U.S. National Archives to trace assets of Holocaust victims still held in Swiss banks. The investigation triggered a reassessment in Switzerland of the country's role in the war.

It was the second document that WJC has found confirming Nazi plans to fund a clandestine postwar network to restore Hitler's political movement to power. Historians and spy novelists have referred to the postwar Nazi network as "Odessa."
In May the WJC released a document saying that Nazi leaders secretly met top German industrialists in 1944 in Strasbourg, France, to plan a postwar industrial network that would return them to power.
The Strasbourg document said that an SS general and a representative of the German armaments industry told the industralists they must be prepared to finance the Nazi party once it went underground.
The latest document has the Nazis, almost a year later, financing themselves under the cover of moving private assets to Swiss banks, which had been helpful to the Germans during the course of war.

The document alleged "The National Socialist Party about the latter part of 1944 formed a secret chancellery of the Nazi party for all foreign countries known as the 'Geheime-Partei-Kanzlei Ausland.' Its purpose is to concentrate and centralize all efforts with a view to effect complete efficiency of the clandestine movement of the party."

The OSS document said that the Nazis were using "the same means of transportation" to bring the party's assets into Switzerland to create a clandestine fund that it had previously employed to transport gold, jewels and foreign securities into Switzerland and other neutral countries.

The document added the funds for the secret network "are to be deposited in neutral countries in the names of dummies and business houses and industrial firms in order to camouflage these activitiies."

It added that the German Reich had dissolved a credit watchdog agency that it described as "the last obstacle confronting the Nazi party which prevented it from seizing savings and bank deposits without a valid explanation."
